transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because the clinic for a logistics job wouldn’t clear me. They said my weight was too low. I don’t really see it that way—I mean, I feel like I’m just lean, ready to work, stay quick on my feet.
Do you think your weight is normal for your height?

I think it’s normal enough for me. My sister and the doctor keep saying I’m in danger, but honestly I think they’re making it bigger than it is. I’m just trying to keep myself light and sharp, ready to work.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah… I guess I am, in a way. If I eat rice or bread, or something greasy, I start thinking it’s going to sit on me right away. Then the next morning I’ll check the scale or my belt, just to make sure I didn’t let myself go.
Do you think you look thin when you look in the mirror?

Not really. I mean, I can see I’m smaller than some men my age, but when I look in the mirror I mostly notice my stomach and my waist. If they don’t look tight, if I’m not smaller there, I feel like I’ve let myself slip… like I’m not the disciplined man I used to be working on the warehouse floor.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ll eat more than I planned sometimes, but I wouldn’t call it a large amount. Usually I’m pretty careful with that.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No… I don’t make myself throw up after eating. That’s not something I do.
Do you ever exercise excessively to burn off calories after eating?
I’m not really sure. I do try to stay active, and I don’t like sitting around after I eat, but I don’t know if I’d call it exercising excessively just to burn it off.
Do you increase your physical activity after eating to try to burn off the calories?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of it that way. I might move around or keep busy after eating, but I haven’t really tracked whether I’m doing it to burn calories.
Do you ever use laxatives or diuretics to try to lose weight?
No, I don’t use laxatives or water pills to lose weight. That’s not something I do.
How often do you think about your weight or body shape in a typical day?

A lot, honestly. It comes up throughout the day. If I catch myself in the mirror, especially my stomach and waist, I start thinking I need to be smaller, tighter-looking. It feels tied up with whether I’m still disciplined, like the man I used to be working on the warehouse floor.
Do you ever feel like you've lost control while eating?
I don’t think so. I mean, I usually feel pretty aware of what I’m eating. I can’t really think of times where I felt like I couldn’t stop or wasn’t in control.
When you think about your body shape or weight, do you think your perception of it is different from how others see you?

Yeah… I think it probably is different. Other people might see me as thin or say I look fine, but when I look in the mirror, I mostly notice my stomach and waist. If I’m not smaller and tight-looking there, it feels like I’m not the disciplined man I used to be working on the warehouse floor.
Have you recently lost a significant amount of weight?

I guess they’re saying I have. I’m here because the clinic for that logistics job wouldn’t clear me — they said my weight was too low. But to me, I don’t really see it that way. I just look lean, like someone who’s ready to work and stay quick on his feet.
When you think about gaining weight, what is it about being heavier that scares you?

I guess I’m scared it’ll show up on me right away. Like if I eat rice or bread, or something greasy, I start thinking it’s just going to sit there on my body. Then the next morning I’ll check the scale or see how my belt feels, just to make sure I didn’t… let myself go.
How would you feel if you gained a small amount of weight, like a few pounds?

Even a few pounds would bother me. I’d feel like it was going to show on me right away, especially if I’d eaten rice or bread or something greasy. I’d probably be thinking about it all night, then check the scale or see how my belt feels in the morning, just to make sure I didn’t let myself go.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an amount of food that is much larger than most people would eat in a short period of time?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’m pretty careful with what I eat, so I can’t really think of times where I ate way more than other people in one sitting.
When you look at yourself, do you see yourself as others see you or do you see a different image of yourself?

I think I see something different. When I look in the mirror, I focus on my stomach and my waist. If I don’t look smaller and kind of tight, I feel like I’m not the disciplined man I used to be, back when I was working on the warehouse floor.
When you look at yourself, do you think your body shape or weight is the same as what others see when they look at you?

No, I don’t think it’s the same. Other people might say I look fine, but when I look in the mirror I go straight to my stomach and waist. If I don’t look smaller, tight, like I used to when I was working the warehouse floor, I feel like I’ve lost that discipline.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is because of how you think you would look or because of something else?

It’s mostly how I think I’ll look, yeah. If I eat rice or bread or something greasy, I start thinking it’s going to sit on me right away. Then the next morning I’ll check the scale or my belt, just to make sure I didn’t let myself go.
